strategy_catalog.name: Enlarged Tile Sizes
strategy_catalog.natural_language: Increase BLOCK_M, BLOCK_N, and BASE_K from 64 to 128. Larger tile sizes amortize loop overhead, improve L0A/L0B utilization from 25% to 50%, and reduce the number of Mmad iterations per tile. This is the most impactful single change for bandwidth-bound attention because each Mmad processes more data, reducing per-tile sync and loop overhead. However, larger tiles require more L1 buffer space for Q (128*dim*2 bytes per buffer) and KV (128*dim*2 bytes per buffer). For dim=128, Q buffer = 128*128*2 = 32KB, KV buffer = 128*128*2 = 32KB, which fits comfortably in 512KB L1. For dim=512, Q buffer = 128*512*2 = 128KB, KV buffer = 128*512*2 = 128KB, total ~384KB including P buffer, which may approach L1 limit.

constraints: BLOCK_M must be multiple of C0 (=16 for fp16)
BLOCK_N must be multiple of C0
BASE_K must be multiple of C0
Q buffer in L1 = BLOCK_M * dim * sizeof(QType) must fit in 512KB - KV_buffer - P_buffer
L0A/L0B dual-buffer: 2 * BLOCK_M * BASE_K * sizeof(half) = 2*128*128*2 = 64KB < 64KB limit per L0A/L0B

strategy_catalog.dsl: TILE_SIZE { BLOCK_M: 128, BLOCK_N: 128, BASE_K: 128 } CONSTRAINT { L0A_buf: 2*BLOCK_M*BASE_K*2 <= 64KB, L1_Q_buf: BLOCK_M*dim*2 <= (512KB - KV_buf - P_buf), alignment: BLOCK_M % C0 == 0, BLOCK_N % C0 == 0 } IMPACT { bandwidth: 9/10, register: 6/10, compute: 7/10 } EXPECT { speedup: [1.5, 2.5] } FILES { tiling.h, kernel.h, cube.h, vec.h }

strategy_catalog.name: WorkspaceQueue Pattern
strategy_catalog.natural_language: Replace raw CrossCoreSetFlag/WaitFlag with a typed WorkspaceQueue class that encapsulates workspace ring-buffer management. WorkspaceQueue provides ProducerAcquire() to get the next slot, ProducerReleaseFix() or ProducerReleaseMte3() to signal completion with the correct pipeline mode, and ConsumerAcquire() which waits with the correct PIPE_MTE2 mode. This ensures that AIC->AIV sync uses the minimal pipeline scope: Fixpipe completion signals S_READY (PIPE_FIX), DataCopy completion signals P_READY (PIPE_MTE3), and AIV consumption uses PIPE_MTE2. This eliminates the mismatch between producer pipeline (FIX for S, MTE3 for P and O) and consumer pipeline (MTE2 for all). The ring buffer slot calculation is encapsulated: slot = (head/tail % RING_SLOTS) * slotSize, eliminating manual offset tracking.
strategy_catalog.dsl: WORKSPACE_QUEUE { T: QType, DEPTH: RING_SLOTS } METHOD { ProducerAcquire: ws_[head_%DEPTH*slotSize_], ProducerReleaseFix: CrossCoreSetFlag<0x2,PIPE_FIX>(notifyId_)+head_++, ProducerReleaseMte3: CrossCoreSetFlag<0x2,PIPE_MTE3>(notifyId_)+head_++, ConsumerAcquire: CrossCoreWaitFlag<0x2,PIPE_MTE2>(notifyId_)+ws_[tail_++%DEPTH*slotSize_] } SIGNALS { S_READY: 0_PIPE_FIX, P_READY: 1_PIPE_MTE3, O_READY: 2_PIPE_FIX } EXPECT { speedup: [1.2, 1.5] } FILES { workspace_queue.h, cube.h, vec.h, kernel.h }

strategy_catalog.name: Q L1 Cache Skip
strategy_catalog.natural_language: Add a Q chunk caching mechanism in the Cube (AIC) side. Track qChunkStart_ (row offset) and qChunkId_ (bz*nq+qHead identifier). When LoadQ is called with the same chunkId and qRowStart, skip the GM->L1 DataCopy entirely and reuse the Q data already in L1. This eliminates redundant Q loads when the same Q tile is reused across multiple KV iterations or micro-M loops. The Q data stays resident in L1 across the entire inner KV loop, reducing GM traffic significantly. For MQA specifically, Q is loaded once per q_outer block but reused for every KV tile, so the savings is proportional to kvSeqLen/BLOCK_N.

cache_logic.update: qChunkStart_ = qRowStart; qChunkId_ = chunkId; qChunkRowsAlign_ = AlignUp(qChunkRows, C0);
cache_logic.skip_condition: Same batch-head-tile identifier means Q is already in L1

strategy_catalog.dsl: CACHE_SKIP { target: Q, fields: [qChunkStart_, qChunkId_, qChunkRowsAlign_], init: 0xffffffff, check: qChunkStart_==qRowStart && qChunkId_==chunkId, update: qChunkStart_=qRowStart; qChunkId_=chunkId; qChunkRowsAlign_=AlignUp(qChunkRows,C0) } BENEFIT { GM_traffic_reduction: proportional to kvSeqLen/BLOCK_N per Q reuse } EXPECT { speedup: [1.05, 1.15] } FILES { cube.h }

strategy_catalog.name: Vectorized RowMuls/RowDivs
strategy_catalog.natural_language:
Replace scalar RowMulsImpl/RowDivsImpl (which use GetValue per-row loops) with vectorized RowMuls/RowDivs helper functions.

Important: RowMuls and RowDivs are NOT AscendC built-in APIs. They are user-defined __aicore__ inline functions that wrap Mul/Div with BinaryRepeatParams to achieve row-wise broadcast scaling at vector width (64 fp16/cycle) instead of scalar width (1/cycle). You must define or import these functions before calling them. Reference implementation: references/row_ops_source_reference/vector_common_row_ops.h

The scalar loops process one element per cycle while the vector unit sits idle. The vectorized helper functions take a scale source tensor and broadcast it across each row of the destination tensor, processing 64 fp16 elements per cycle. Similarly RowDivs divides each row by the corresponding element from a source tensor.

This change requires: (1) In Vec2, prepare a scale tensor (expStateUb) from softmax state cache; (2) Call RowMuls(oPrevUb, oPrevUb, expStateUb, dealRows, dim, actualDim) where the 4th argument is the number of rows, 5th is aligned dim, and 6th is actual dim; (3) Call RowDivs(oNewUb, oNewUb, sumStateUb, dealRows, dim, actualDim) for final normalization. The state tensors must be properly sized: each row's scale factor is at offset row*BRCB_NUM in the state buffer.

VEC2_row_ops.RowMuls: RowMuls(oPrevUb_, oPrevUb_, expStateUb, dealRows, dim, actualDim)
VEC2_row_ops.RowDivs: RowDivs(oNewUb, oNewUb, sumStateUb, dealRows, dim, actualDim)

strategy_catalog.dsl: ROW_OPS { mode: vectorized, ops: [RowMuls, RowDivs], src: expStateUb/sumStateUb, params: {dealRows, dim, actualDim} } BROADCAST { BRCB_NUM: 32/sizeof(float), stride: AlignUp(subBlockRows_*BRCB_NUM*4,32)/4 } BUF_ALLOC { maxCacheBuf_: TBuf<VECCALC> RING_SLOTS*stride*4, sumCacheBuf_: TBuf<VECCALC> RING_SLOTS*stride*4, expCacheBuf_: TBuf<VECCALC> RING_SLOTS*stride*4 } EXPECT { speedup: [1.1, 1.3] } FILES { vec.h }

api_references.summary: RowMuls不是AscendC框架内置API，而是用户自定义__aicore__ inline函数。签名: RowMuls(dstUb, src0Ub, src1Ub, dealRowCount, columnCount, actualColumnCount)。底层实现: Mul(dst,src0,src1,count,repeatTimes,BinaryRepeatParams{src1BlkStride=0,src1RepStride=1})实现每行用同一BRCB_BLOCK缩放。使用前必须定义此函数（源码参考: references/row_ops_source_reference/vector_common_row_ops.h）。scale参数是LocalTensor[dealRowCount,BRCB_NUM(=8)]而非float标量。

anti_patterns.reason: PIPE_V RAW冒险(Duplicate写buf后Mul立即读同一PIPE_V无PipeBarrier) + padding区域垃圾值不清零(Duplicate仅填充dim个位置, Mul操作整个dimAlign宽度) + 累积精度误差(1次额外Duplicate赋值舍入ε)

anti_patterns.pattern: LocalTensor[] 下标运算符作为 float 标量参数传入 Muls
anti_patterns.reason: LocalTensor[] 返回子张量视图 LocalTensor<T>，不是标量 T。使用 GetValue(tensor, index) 提取标量值。

anti_patterns.pattern: Brcb(dst,src,count) 只传3个参数替代 RowMuls
anti_patterns.reason: AscendC Brcb 需要4个参数: Brcb(dst,src,repeatTimes,dstStride)。Mulcs在CANN 9.0中不存在(应为Muls)。正确的行级广播乘法是RowMuls函数(Mul+BinaryRepeatParams)。

anti_patterns.pattern: 直接调用RowMuls而不先定义该函数
anti_patterns.reason: RowMuls不是AscendC框架内置API，是用户自定义函数。调用前必须在项目中定义此函数(参考vector_common_row_ops.h源码)，否则编译失败(undeclared)。

api_references.summary: RowDivs不是AscendC框架内置API，而是用户自定义__aicore__ inline函数。签名: RowDivs(dstUb, src0Ub, src1Ub, dealRowCount, columnCount, actualColumnCount)。底层实现: Div(dst,src0,src1,count,repeatTimes,BinaryRepeatParams{src1BlkStride=0,src1RepStride=1})。使用前必须定义此函数（源码参考: references/row_ops_source_reference/vector_common_row_ops.h）。

anti_patterns.pattern: 直接调用RowDivs而不先定义该函数
anti_patterns.reason: RowDivs不是AscendC框架内置API。调用前必须定义或引入包含该函数的头文件。

api_references.doc_path: api_reference_docs/基础API/矢量计算/基础算术/Mul.md
api_references.summary: Mul(dst, src0, src1, count) 或 Mul(dst, src0, src1, mask, repeatTimes, repeatParams)。高维切分模式通过BinaryRepeatParams控制src0/src1/dst的stride，实现行级广播缩放。RowMuls底层即用此API。

api_references.doc_path: api_reference_docs/基础API/矢量计算/基础算术/Div.md
api_references.summary: Div(dst, src0, src1, count) 或 Div(dst, src0, src1, mask, repeatTimes, repeatParams)。高维切分模式与Mul对称。RowDivs底层即用此API。

BinaryRepeatParams控制双源矢量算子(Mul/Div/Add等)高维切分模式的stride参数。关键字段: src0BlkStride, src1BlkStride, dstBlkStride(block内stride), src0RepStride, src1RepStride, dstRepStride(repeat间stride)。RowMuls关键配置: src1BlkStride=0(src1连续读取), src1RepStride=1(每repeat前进1block=8个fp32)。
GetValue(index: uint32) → PrimType. 获取LocalTensor指定索引的标量值。仅在VECIN/VECCALC/VECOUT位置支持。用于从LocalTensor提取float标量（而非[]下标运算符）。
Duplicate(dst, src, count). 广播复制：将src单个元素复制count次到dst。仅填充count个有效元素，padding区域(dimAlign-dim)保留垃圾值不清零。
Brcb(dst, src, repeatTimes, dstStride). 需要4参数，不可只传3个。用于行级广播复制。

strategy_catalog.name: VEC2 Large Chunk
strategy_catalog.natural_language: Increase VEC2_M_CHUNK from 8 to 64. Vec2 processes O accumulation in row chunks; larger chunks amortize loop overhead and allow RowMuls/RowDivs to operate on more rows at once, improving vector unit utilization. VEC2_M_CHUNK=64 means processing BLOCK_M rows in a single chunk when BLOCK_M=128, or in two chunks when BLOCK_M=128 with subBlockRows_=64. UB budget check: oPrevBuf needs VEC2_M_CHUNK * dimAlign * sizeof(float) = 64*128*4 = 32KB for dim=128, which fits in UB alongside other buffers (total UB ~196KB).
strategy_catalog.dsl: VEC2_CHUNK { VEC2_M_CHUNK: 64 } UB_CHECK { oPrevBuf: 64*dimAlign*4 <= (196KB - other_bufs) } EXPECT { speedup: [1.05, 1.15] } FILES { vec.h }

strategy_catalog.name: Softmax UB State Cache
strategy_catalog.natural_language: Cache softmax max/sum/exp states per ring slot in UB (maxCacheBuf_, sumCacheBuf_, expCacheBuf_) instead of writing them to GM workspace (wsMeta). Each slot has a stateStride of AlignUp(subBlockRows_*BRCB_NUM*4, 32)/4 float elements. In Vec1, instead of writing meta to wsMetaGm, write to maxCacheUb[slot*stateStride], sumCacheUb[slot*stateStride], expCacheUb[slot*stateStride]. In Vec2, instead of reading from wsMetaGm, read from the cached UB state. This eliminates GM round-trips for softmax state per KV tile, saving ~BLOCK_M*3*4 bytes per tile of GM traffic. The default state buffers (softmaxMaxDefaultBuf_, softmaxSumDefaultBuf_) are initialized with -inf/0 and reused for isFirst=true cases.
strategy_catalog.dsl: SOFTMAX_STATE_CACHE { location: UB, stride: AlignUp(subBlockRows_*BRCB_NUM*4,32)/4, slots: RING_SLOTS, default: {max: -1e9, sum: 0} } BUF_ALLOC { maxCacheBuf_: TBuf<VECCALC> RING_SLOTS*stride*4, sumCacheBuf_: TBuf<VECCALC> RING_SLOTS*stride*4, expCacheBuf_: TBuf<VECCALC> RING_SLOTS*stride*4 } EXPECT { speedup: [1.05, 1.1] } FILES { vec.h }

strategy_catalog.name: Sub-block Row Handling
strategy_catalog.natural_language: Properly handle AIV sub-block processing. In MIX_AIC_1_2 mode, each Cube core has 2 Vector sub-blocks. Each sub-block processes its own rows: subBlockRows_ = BLOCK_M / subBlockNum_, rowStart_ = subBlockIdx_ * subBlockRows_. In Vec1, each subblock reads only its rows from the S workspace slot (offset = rowStart_ * BLOCK_N), processes softmax on curSubBlockRows_ rows, and writes P back to the corresponding offset. This ensures no cross-subblock data races and proper vector width utilization. The inputQue1/outputQue1 buffer sizes are based on subBlockRows_ instead of BLOCK_M, reducing UB pressure.

ub_savings.inputBuf: subBlockRows_ * BLOCK_N * 4 instead of BLOCK_M * BLOCK_N * 4
ub_savings.outputBuf: subBlockRows_ * BLOCK_N * 2 instead of BLOCK_M * BLOCK_N * 2

strategy_catalog.dsl: SUB_BLOCK { subBlockNum: GetSubBlockNum(), subBlockIdx: GetSubBlockIdx(), subBlockRows: BLOCK_M/subBlockNum, rowStart: subBlockIdx*subBlockRows } BUF_SIZE { inputQue: subBlockRows*BLOCK_N*4, outputQue: subBlockRows*BLOCK_N*2 } EXPECT { speedup: [1.02, 1.08] } FILES { vec.h }

strategy_catalog.name: Targeted SetWaitFlag
strategy_catalog.natural_language: Replace all PipeBarrier<PIPE_ALL> with targeted SetWaitFlag<HardEvent::X_Y> calls. PipeBarrier<PIPE_ALL> drains all pipeline channels (V, M, MTE1, MTE2, MTE3, FIX), destroying overlap. Targeted barriers only wait for the specific dependency needed. In Cube: use SetWaitFlag<HardEvent::M_MTE1> before loading data from L1 to L0 (depends on MTE1 completing); SetWaitFlag<HardEvent::MTE1_M> before Mmad (depends on MTE1 completing); SetWaitFlag<HardEvent::M_FIX> before Fixpipe (depends on Mmad completing); SetWaitFlag<HardEvent::FIX_MTE2> after Fixpipe (allows L0C reuse). In Vector: use SetWaitFlag<HardEvent::MTE3_MTE2> before DataCopy from GM to UB; SetWaitFlag<HardEvent::MTE2_V> before vector compute; SetWaitFlag<HardEvent::V_MTE3> before DataCopy from UB to GM; SetWaitFlag<HardEvent::MTE3_V> after GM write completion. Each targeted barrier preserves pipeline overlap for unrelated channels.
strategy_catalog.dsl: BARRIER { cube: { M_MTE1: before_LoadData_L0, MTE1_M+PIPE_M: before_Mmad, M_FIX: before_Fixpipe, FIX_MTE2: after_Fixpipe }, vector: { MTE3_MTE2: before_DataCopy_GM2UB, MTE2_V: before_vec_compute, PIPE_V: after_vec_compute, V_MTE3: before_DataCopy_UB2GM, MTE3_V: after_GM_write } } REPLACE { PipeBarrier<PIPE_ALL> -> targeted_SetWaitFlag } EXPECT { speedup: [1.2, 1.5] } FILES { cube.h, vec.h }

strategy_catalog.name: oPrev Dedicated TBuf
strategy_catalog.natural_language: Allocate a dedicated TBuf<VECCALC> oPrevBuf_ for Vec2 O accumulation instead of using a TQue slot. This avoids consuming a TQue slot while oNewUb is live, keeping peak UB within limits. The buffer size is VEC2_M_CHUNK * dimAlign * sizeof(float). In Vec2, when !isFirst, DataCopy wsAccOGm to oPrevUb_ (the dedicated TBuf), then RowMuls oPrevUb_ with expState, then Add oNewUb += oPrevUb_. This eliminates the need for double-buffering the accumulation in TQue, freeing UB space for other buffers.
strategy_catalog.dsl: DEDICATED_BUF { name: oPrevBuf_, type: TBuf<VECCALC>, size: VEC2_M_CHUNK*dimAlign*4, tensor: oPrevUb_ = oPrevBuf_.Get<float>() } USAGE { DataCopy(wsAccOGm->oPrevUb_), RowMuls(oPrevUb_,oPrevUb_,expState), Add(oNewUb+=oPrevUb_) } EXPECT { speedup: [1.02, 1.05] } FILES { vec.h }

strategy_catalog.name: Multi-level KV Outer Tiling
strategy_catalog.natural_language: Implement a two-level KV sequence tiling scheme with s2OuterBlocks and s2BaseSize. When kvSeqLen is large, split it into s2OuterBlocks outer blocks of size s2BaseSize. Each outer block contains microNLoops = CeilDiv(s2Rows, BLOCK_N) inner micro-tiles. The outer loop iterates over s2OuterBlocks, and the inner loop iterates over microNLoops micro-tiles within each outer block. This enables: (1) Q can be loaded once at the start of each outer block and reused across all inner micro-tiles; (2) tileBase accumulation across outer blocks enables correct Vec1/Vec2 slot indexing; (3) Better L1 reuse patterns because Q stays resident across all KV inner tiles within an outer block. The s2OuterBlocks and s2BaseSize are computed in host tiling based on kvSeqLen and available core count.

s2OuterBlocks.source: computed in host tiling from kvSeqLen and s2BaseSize

s2BaseSize.description: Outer KV block size in rows

structured_params.q_residency: LoadQ once per (bz, qHead, qRowStart, qRows); reuse across all inner micro-tiles

strategy_catalog.dsl: OUTER_TILING { s2OuterBlocks: ceil(kvSeqLen/s2BaseSize), s2BaseSize: from_host_tiling } LOOP { outer: for(s2OuterIdx=0;s2OuterIdx<s2OuterBlocks), inner: for(t=0;t<microNLoops+PRELAUNCH) } Q_RESIDENCY { load_once_per_outer_block, reuse_across_inner_tiles } TILE_BASE { accumulate: tileBase+=microNLoops } EXPECT { speedup: [1.3, 2.0] } FILES { tiling.h, tiling.cpp, kernel.h, cube.h }

strategy_catalog.name: Single KV L1 Buffer
strategy_catalog.natural_language: Use a single kvBufL1_ (TBuf<A1>) for K and a single vBufL1_ (TBuf<A1>) for V, instead of double-buffered kBufL1_0/1 and vBufL1_0/1. The WorkspaceQueue pattern with targeted sync (PIPE_FIX for S, PIPE_MTE3 for P) ensures that AIC doesn't need to overlap K/V prefetch with computation — the AIC->AIV pipeline sync is handled by the queue. Since each KV tile is loaded, consumed in MM1/MM2, and then the workspace slot is released, there's no need for double-buffering at L1 level. This saves 2*BLOCK_N*dim*sizeof(QType) bytes of L1 space (one slot per buffer type), which can be used for larger Q chunks or P buffers.
strategy_catalog.dsl: SINGLE_BUF { kvBufL1_: TBuf<A1> BLOCK_N*dim*sizeof(QType), vBufL1_: TBuf<A1> BLOCK_N*dim*sizeof(QType) } REMOVE { kBufL1_0, kBufL1_1, vBufL1_0, vBufL1_1 } L1_SAVINGS { 2*BLOCK_N*dim*sizeof(QType) } RATIONALE { WorkspaceQueue_sync_eliminates_need_for_L1_double_buffer } EXPECT { speedup: [1.05, 1.15] } FILES { cube.h }

strategy_catalog.name: KV Remain Handling
strategy_catalog.natural_language: Handle dim values that are not divisible by BASE_K with kRemain/nRemain loops. In MM1, after the main ki loop (dim/BASE_K iterations), check kRemain = dim % BASE_K. If kRemain > 0, do one extra Mmad iteration with kAligned = AlignUp(kRemain, C0) as the K dimension, setting cmatrix_init_val based on whether kTiles was 0. In MM2, similarly handle nRemain = dim % BASE_K with an extra Mmad iteration for the remaining output columns, using FixpipeNzL0cToNdGm for the non-standard N dimension. This ensures correctness for all dim values (not just multiples of BASE_K) and avoids silent precision loss from ignoring the remainder.
strategy_catalog.dsl: REMAIN_LOOP { MM1: { kRemain: dim%BASE_K, kAligned: AlignUp(kRemain,C0), cmatrix_init: kTiles==0 }, MM2: { nRemain: dim%BASE_K, nAligned: AlignUp(nRemain,C0), cmatrix_init: true, Fixpipe: NzL0cToNdGm } } CORRECTNESS { ensures_all_dim_values_handled } EXPECT { speedup: [1.0, 1.05] } FILES { cube.h }
